body:
Thanks for the PR! Unfortunately, I don't think this is a good idea:

1. The `deprecated` and `experimental` marks are still part of the documentation system and don't exist in the core API (like `ClassDB`).
2. This is inconsistent with other doc comment tags (`## @tutorial`). Should we add the `@brief`, `@description`, and `@tutorial` annotations as well?
3. This creates duplicate functionality and compatibility issues. Doc comment tags should continue to work for compatibility reasons and will remain the preferred option for addon authors, since older Godot versions only support them, and unknown annotations cause parser errors. What if someone uses both doc comment tags and the new annotations at the same time? This prevents consistency when you have more than one way to do the same thing.
4. While some languages ​​use the `deprecated` annotation/attribute at the language level, `@tags` in doc comments are generally common in documentation systems (like JavaDoc). The `deprecated` and `experimental` marks in Godot support BBCode markup, as do the main parts of doc comments (brief and description). We could potentially add highlighting and autocompletion for BBCode in doc comments.

In my opinion, leaving things as is makes more sense. The `deprecated` annotation/attribute at the language level makes sense for general-purpose languages ​​that want to allow deprecation of class members independently of third-party documentation systems implemented through doc comments. However, GDScript is a domain-specific language that is highly integrated into Godot. It has the only official documentation system, so the language can parse doc comments directly. Supporting aliases as annotations doesn't solve any pressing problem, but rather introduces new ones due to style variability and incompatibility with older versions.
